hook.en: Testing tiny involuntary joint movements ('joint play') that you cannot do by yourself, to find out if a joint is blocked.
hook.ur: Mennell joint play mein joint ke chhote passive glides ya spins check kiye jate hain jo patient khud active movement se nahi kar sakta.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Mennell Joint-Play Approach is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (4 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Mennell Joint-Play Approach kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 4 checks.)

text.en: Joint play (Mennell) means the small, passive give inside a joint, such as a slight glide or spin, which allows normal movement. If it is lost, normal movement may be restricted or painful. You test each joint's play, compare sides, and treat if it is reduced.
text.ur: Joint play joint ke andar chhoti passive give ko kehte hain, jaise halka glide ya spin, jo normal movement mein hissa leta hai. Agar yeh kam ho to movement restricted ya painful ho sakti hai. Joint play test karke sides compare ki jati hain; treatment tab consider hota hai jab finding relevant ho.

simpler.en: Testing tiny involuntary joint movements ('joint play') that you cannot do by yourself, to find out if a joint is blocked.
simpler.ur: Mennell joint play mein joint ke chhote passive glides ya spins check kiye jate hain jo patient khud active movement se nahi kar sakta.

text.en: A door hinge needs a tiny bit of wiggle to swing smoothly. If the hinge has no wiggle, the door sticks even though the door itself is fine.
text.ur: Darwaze ke hinge ko smoothly swing karne ke liye halki si wiggle chahiye. Wiggle na ho to darwaza atak sakta hai, chahe darwaza khud theek ho. Yeh sirf analogy hai.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Joint play cannot be performed actively; you must test it passively with the joint relaxed.
**2.** Test in a loose-packed position, compare to the other side, and look for lost or painful play.
**3.** Reduced joint play is one finding to interpret alongside pain and function.
text.ur: Joint play active taur par nahi ki ja sakti; relaxed joint par passive test hota hai. Loose-packed position mein test karke doosri side se compare karein aur lost ya painful movement note karein. Reduced joint play ek finding hai jise pain aur function ke sath samajhna chahiye.

text.en:
So when does **Mennell Joint-Play Approach** make sense?
• A joint with restricted movement and no clear tissue cause.
• As part of an orthopedic examination.
text.ur: Restricted movement walay joint mein jab tissue cause clear na ho, ya orthopedic examination ke hissa ke taur par. Fracture, infection ya instability mein na karein; aur agar test se pain sharply barhe to rok dein.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Fractures, infection, or instability.
• Joint play testing that increases pain sharply.
**Stop rule:** Avoid accessory stress where acute fracture, dislocation, significant instability or active inflammatory joint pathology is suspected.
text.ur: Normal variation ko pathology kehna, force barha kar mobility 'prove' karna aur symptom response ignore karna avoid karein. Relevant precautions screen karein aur test ke baad patient ke comparable movement ko dobara check karein.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Position in loose-pack
steps.detail: Support the joint so muscles relax.

steps.title: Glide the other bone
steps.detail: Apply a gentle glide, traction or compression.

steps.title: Decide
steps.detail: Reduced play with a link to the patient's problem supports treatment.

steps.title: Treat and retest
steps.detail: Mobilize if appropriate and recheck the movement.

beats.ur:
1. Joint ko loose-packed position mein support karein taake muscles relax hon.
2. Ek bone ko stabilize karein.
3. Doosri bone ko gentle glide, traction ya compression dein.
4. Doosri side se amount, end-feel aur pain compare karein.
5. Dekhein reduced play patient ke problem se linked hai ya nahi.
6. Munasib ho to mobilize karke movement dobara check karein.

beats.patient: Hannah, 36, wrist pain after a cast was removed; wrist extension is limited.
beats.assessment: Joint play at the radiocarpal joint is reduced compared with the other wrist.
beats.treatment: A gentle glide mobilization is applied, followed by active movement.
beats.reassess: Wrist extension improves. She continues home exercises.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Source mein Hannah, 36 saal ki, cast utarne ke baad wrist pain aur limited extension rakhti hai. Radiocarpal joint play doosri wrist ke muqablay mein kam hai. Gentle glide aur active movement ke baad extension improve hoti hai; home exercises jari rehti hain. Yeh teaching scenario hai.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Testing in a tense position.
• Forgetting to compare sides.
• Treating a finding that does not match the patient's complaint.
**Myth to drop:** 'My thumbs can tell you exactly which microscopic joint surface is wrong.' No reliable magic microscope exists.
text.ur: Tense position mein test karna; sides compare na karna; ya aisi finding treat karna jo patient ki complaint se match na karti ho.

question.en: Can the patient do joint play on their own?
question.ur: Can the patient do joint play on their own?

answer.en: No, it must be tested passively.
answer.ur: No, it must be tested passively.

text.en:
Joint-play testing is a classic examination concept. Reliability varies, so findings should be linked to symptoms and function rather than used alone.
This is an influential historical manual therapy concept. Do not infer that a palpated restriction identifies exact pathology or that a Mennell-branded manipulation is superior.
text.ur: Joint ki passive glide check karein, sides compare karein aur function se link karein. Joint-play testing classic examination concept hai, magar reliability vary karti hai; isay akelay use na karein.
